set.body:
# Loop planner and kernels

Authority: PRD.json 0.1.0, release target 1.0.

## Objective
Implement broadcasting, loop planning, primitive elementwise kernels, comparisons, and generic callback maps.

## Product requirements

## RAV-BCAST-001 [must]
Broadcasting shall align trailing axes and use NumPy-compatible dimension rules without implementing the result as max(left, right).

Acceptance:
- Equal dimensions produce that dimension.
- A dimension of 1 expands to the other dimension.
- Dimensions 0 and 1 broadcast to 0.
- All other unequal dimension pairs fail.
- The expanded operand receives stride zero.
- A mismatch reports both original shapes and the first incompatible aligned axis.

## RAV-API-003 [must]
Ravel 1.0 shall provide the agreed eager pointwise numerical and comparison operations.

Acceptance:
- Arithmetic dtypes support unary plus and minus, same-dtype add, subtract, multiply, divide, scalar arithmetic, and abs.
- Ordered numeric dtypes support minimum, maximum, clip, less-than, and less-than-or-equal operations.
- Floating dtypes support sqrt, exp, log, sin, cos, tan, floor, ceil, isNaN, and isFinite.
- Elementwise equality uses an explicit array operator or method rather than overriding ordinary Scala ==.
- Comparisons allocate Boolean arrays.

## RAV-EXEC-001 [must]
Ordinary numerical syntax shall execute eagerly and allocate one output per operation.

Acceptance:
- Ravel core contains no lazy expression graph, JIT compiler, automatic-differentiation tape, or backend registry.
- An expression such as x * y + b may allocate an intermediate in 1.0.
- Allocation behavior is documented rather than hidden behind reshape or view operations.

## RAV-EXEC-002 [must]
The loop planner shall classify validated operations into linear contiguous, scalar broadcast, simple inner-strided, or fully general strided plans.

Acceptance:
- Ranks are aligned before broadcast strides are assigned.
- Length-one axes may be removed.
- Other adjacent axes coalesce only when every operand and output is contiguous across the boundary or both relevant operand strides are zero.
- All products and derived offsets use checked Long arithmetic.
- The fully general loop uses counters and physical offsets rather than repeated division of a linear index.

## RAV-EXEC-003 [must]
Built-in numerical kernels shall be pure and monomorphic; callback-based map APIs shall retain observable Scala callback semantics.

Acceptance:
- Pure built-in kernels may use lawful reindexing and fusion transformations.
- map, zipMap, mapInto, and zipMapInto invoke callbacks once per logical output element in logical row-major order.
- Callback-based operations are not fused or reordered.
- Callback-based operations make no no-boxing guarantee.
- An exception from a callback stops evaluation and prevents an incomplete allocated output from being returned.

## Deliverables
- Axis coalescing and plan classification.
- Contiguous, scalar-broadcast, inner-strided, and general strided loops.
- Fill, copy, unary arithmetic, binary arithmetic, and comparison kernels.
- map and zipMap with explicit callback evaluation semantics.

## Exit criteria
- Built-in primitive loops satisfy the Phase 0 structural performance contract.
- Broadcasting handles 0 with 1 as dimension 0.
- Specialized kernels agree with the reference implementation over generated layouts.
- Callback order and exception tests pass.

## Required law coverage
BroadcastLaws and KernelLaws, including the pure-map reindexing law only for total pure functions.

## Relevant risk
RISK-005. Generic callbacks retain once-per-element logical row-major evaluation and receive no no-boxing promise.

## Completion rule
Close this epic only when every listed requirement and exit criterion has executable evidence on every promised platform. Record implementation commits, tests, compiler-output evidence, and any accepted deviation in mote notes.
